newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGB futures end up, investor buying detected.
newsitem.headline: JGB futures end up, investor buying detected.

text.p: Key June Japanese government bond (JGB) futures ended Friday's Tokyo session higher as investors bought cash JGBs, traders said.
The benchmark contract closed up 0.10 at 125.50, after trading between 125.31 and 125.68. Turnover was 47,001 lots.
"Cash JGBs, not futures, dominated activity today. The market's mood has improved as investors' buying was detected," said a trader at a city bank's securities unit.
"Dealers were also actively squaring up short positions in cash JGBs, such as the benchmark 182nd JGB, ahead of the long weekend," he added.
June futures extended gains in early afternoon but were capped by heavy offers at around 125.70.
"Market participants saw 125.70 as the key technical point. June could have squeezed even higher if this level was breached," said a trader at another city bank's securities unit.
Traders said life insurance companies were detected buying cash JGBs at the long-end of the yield curve, such as 190th to 194th JGBs, while selling the intermediate sector.
"Life insurers have been seen buying at the long-end since yesterday," said the first trader.
Traders said some public fund bodies were also seen buying 193rd and 194th JGBs.
A relatively stable yen/dollar exchange rate was also positive for JGBs today, traders said.
The dollar was quoted at around 126.70/80 yen as of 3.45 p.m. (0645 GMT), compared with 126.55/60 yen on late Thursday in New York.
"As long as the yen/dollar remains below 127 yen, there should not be any problem for JGBs," said a brokerage house trader. Gains in Tokyo stocks had a limited impact on JGBs, traders said.
The Nikkei 225 stock average ended up 239.42 points, or 1.24 percent, at 19,514.75.
In the morning session, June JGB futures temporarily erased earlier gains following the release of Japan's unemployment rate for March, which showed a slight decline.
The seasonally-adjusted unemployment rate fell to 3.2 percent in March from 3.3 percent in February.
Traders say sentiment in the JGB market has turned more optimistic compared with earlier in the week, but players are still cautious ahead of the release of U.S. employment data for April on Friday.
Economists polled by Reuters forecast, on average, non-farm payrolls to increase 211,000 in April, after a gain of 175,000 in March.
"June JGB futures could test higher next week. If resistance at 125.70 breaks, June could rise above 126.00," said the brokerage house trader.
The yield of the benchmark 182nd JGB stood at 2.295 percent as of 4.05 p.m. (0705 GMT), down from 2.325 percent on Thursday.
Japan's financial markets will be closed on Monday for a national holiday. -- Tokyo Treasury Desk +81-3-3432-9780
